name: Printing
notes:
SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 (Talha, live with Mofeed): full real tier table given directly, replacing the old fixed-100-plus-4-tier guess. No fixed setup cost in this version - verified at 125,000 sheets: (125000/1000)*75 = 9,375 vs Mofeed's real 9,350 (25 SAR off, essentially exact). Tiers (SAR per 1000 sheets): 0-1,000=450, 1,001-3,000=200, 3,001-5,000=180, 5,001-10,000=125, 10,001-50,000=90, 50,001-100,000=80, 100,001+=75.

notes: Mofeed's own words: '15 halala per centimetre' - only matches his real quoted ~360 SAR as an AREA rate (die 53x45cm = 2385 cm2 x 0.15 = 357.75), not a linear one. Confirmed by testing both interpretations against his real number.

name: Cutting
notes:
Confirmed by Talha with 5 real data points (1,000/5,000/10,000/50,000/100,000 pieces = 150/350/550/2,000/3,000 SAR). Fixed 50 SAR + tiered rate exactly reproduces all 5 points. Same table used for BOTH Cutting and Glue (Mofeed's own statement - identical pricing structure for both). Glue's 'extra per side' rule is STILL UNCONFIRMED - Talha described '10 SAR per side per 1000' but that doesn't reproduce his own worked example (2-side, 5000pcs = 600 SAR) - working backward suggests the real per-side rate is closer to 50, not 10. Left as single-side pricing only until clarified - do NOT apply a side multiplier without confirming the real formula.

UPDATE 2026-08-19 (Talha): confirmed the tiered piece-quantity numbers above under-account for Ups per Sheet on real jobs - a 500,000pc/4-up job was computing 14,800 SAR, way too high. Binding layer (cost_driver_binding.py) now divides the computed Cutting cost by doc.ups before it lands on the estimate. NOT yet re-confirmed against a real Mofeed number at ups!=1 - the tier breakpoints themselves are still the original single-up-implied figures. Re-verify with him on the next real multi-up job.

name: Packing
notes:
CONFIRMED PERMANENT DESIGN (Talha, 2026-08-19): Mofeed picks the box size by eye per job - no fixed rule, not weight-only, not a lookup table. This is NOT a temporary gap to close later; a formula would be actively wrong here. Manual override (with a documented reason per job) is the correct, final approach for Packing, same as any job where the real process is human judgement rather than a calculation.

PREVIOUS: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 (Talha, live with Mofeed): real packing formula, not a flat guess. Cartons = (Sheets Required x Sheet Size's A4-Equivalent Count x GSM / 100) / Print Suite Settings' Sheets per Carton. Cost = cartons x this driver's Rate (1.4 SAR/carton). Verified exactly against his real worked example: 125,000 sheets, 70x100 sheet (8 A4-equivalents), 300gsm, 3000 sheets/carton -> 1,000 cartons x 1.4 = 1,400 SAR, matching his real number exactly.

PREVIOUS (kept for reference): Flat 50 SAR, confirmed. Was mislabelled 'Rolling' in an earlier misread of Mofeed's handwriting - corrected directly by Talha.

name: Lamination
notes: Confirmed by Talha with Mofeed's real numbers, 2026-08-19: 0.80 SAR/sheet at 1,000 sheets, sliding down as volume grows to a floor of 0.55 SAR/sheet at 150,000 sheets - the floor never goes lower no matter how large the job. Only 2 real confirmed points, so the cost between them is modelled as a straight-line interpolation (see cost_driver_engine._linear_decline_rate) rather than invented tier breakpoints - the least assumption-laden model given the data we actually have. If Mofeed gives intermediate confirmed points later, worth checking whether the real curve is actually linear or bends.
